phase_name: Re-Arm the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint -- Widen Its Trigger Predicate

objectives.description: Hoist deploy_pending_any computation out of matched_count>0 branch
Adjust announcement to name deploy_pending reason instead of misleading 0-path line
Preserve routing through deploy_ledger_decide and deployed_critical_paths guard
Confirm no edit outside checkpoint block

phase_notes:
Hoisted deploy_pending_any (and a new deploy_pending_tasks_json accumulator, for the announcement) to right after matched_count is computed, still inside the outer `if cycle_modified_files_json != []` gate (left untouched per scope discipline -- Phase 1 already confirmed cycle_modified_files accumulates whenever deploy_pending would be true, so this outer gate does not exclude the realistic case). Widened the branch condition to `{ matched_count -gt 0 || deploy_pending_any = true } && dry_run != true`. Announcement now branches three ways: matched-only (unchanged original text), deploy_pending-only (new: names the triggering task(s), never prints the misleading 'touched 0' line), and both (adds a supplementary 'ALSO triggered by' line). Concurrency posture recorded in-script, citing SKILL.md Move 2's one-message parallel dispatch and the fail-open specs/.deploy-lock mutex, matching the plan's argued conclusion (defer to checkpoint boundary, no new deploy-trigger site).

Diff confined to lines ~756-819 of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, inside the checkpoint block (~695-961) -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` (single file, 63 insertions/22 deletions) and reading the diff directly.

Test coverage: (a) scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh Group 11 gained case (s) -- the direct mechanical test of the widened predicate itself (matched_count==0, deploy_pending_any=true, via a non-allowlisted agent-system/extensions/** path), asserting the deploy body fires, the announcement names its own reason, no misleading 'touched 0' line appears, cycle_modified_files still resets, and the ledger is genuinely consulted (not bypassed) -- 248/248 green. (b) scripts/tests/test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh gained Case 8 -- a stale-then-fresh sequence on update-task-status.sh's own gate proving it is not sticky (a second call after the recorded source_git_head is synced, simulating what the checkpoint's redeploy does in production, succeeds) -- 23/23 green. This is a considered interpretation of the plan's Files-to-modify note (which names test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh for Phase 3's own refusal-then-recovery case): the checkpoint's widened-predicate MECHANICS live in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and are properly tested in that script's own suite (Group 11), while test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh -- which only drives update-task-status.sh directly and has no visibility into orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh at all -- gained the closest in-scope analog: proof that the gate re-evaluates freshness per call rather than latching, which is the property the checkpoint's redeploy-then-retry design depends on. All three suites (test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh 248/248, test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh 110/110, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh 23/23) green together.
